content.question: How does LIME build its explanation for a specific prediction?
options: It computes the gradients of the prediction with respect to the input features and ranks their magnitudes as importance scores.
It retrains the model on modified copies of the training data and measures how much each feature changes the loss.
It perturbs the input locally, observes the predictions on the perturbed samples, and fits a weighted linear surrogate model around the prediction.
It fits one global linear surrogate model to the whole dataset and uses its coefficients to explain every prediction.
It perturbs individual neurons instead of the input, observes which ones most affect the output, and reports them as attributions.
content.answer: It perturbs the input locally, observes the predictions on the perturbed samples, and fits a weighted linear surrogate model around the prediction.
